Calah
KAY-lah
proper noun
Hebrew Kelach, one of the ancient cities of Asshur, a great city of the Assyrian heartland founded in the days of Nimrod.

📖 Biblical Definition

Calah rises in the table of nations among the first cities of the world’s first empire. Out of the land of Shinar “went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh, and the city Rehoboth, and Calah” (Gen 10:11), “and Resen between Nineveh and Calah: the same is a great city” (Gen 10:12). Behind these foundations stands the shadow of Nimrod: “And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth” (Gen 10:8), the mighty hunter whose kingdom began at Babel. Calah was thus a jewel of the Assyrian crown, and Assyria became the rod of God’s anger against His faithless people and a byword for cruelty. Of its capital the prophet cried, “Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery” (Nah 3:1). Calah shows the double truth of the great pagan city: it is a wonder of human building and a monument of human pride, raised in the line of Nimrod who made a name against heaven. The empires of Shinar and Asshur were permitted their hour, used by God to chasten and then themselves broken. The great city that seems eternal is grass; the LORD who raised Assyria to smite Israel afterward laid Nineveh and Calah in the dust. The mighty hunter’s cities do not outlast the word of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

An ancient city of Assyria founded in the line of Nimrod (Gen 10:11-12); a monument of imperial pride raised up and then broken by the God who rules the nations.

CALAH, one of the ancient cities of Asshur in the Assyrian heartland.

Built after the going forth from Shinar, near Nineveh (Gen 10:11).

Set with Resen between Nineveh and Calah, a great city (Gen 10:12).

Standing in the shadow of Nimrod, the mighty hunter (Gen 10:8).

A monument of empire raised and then laid low by God (Nah 3:1).

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 10:11 — "Out of that land went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh, and the city Rehoboth, and Calah,"

Gen 10:12 — "And Resen between Nineveh and Calah: the same is a great city."

Gen 10:8 — "And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth."

Nah 3:1 — "Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

An ancient Assyrian city of Nimrod’s line; the entry recovers that the proudest empire is raised for its hour and then broken by the God of the nations.

expand to see more

Calah’s abiding lesson is the vanity of empire. Founded in the line of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one and built Babel, it belonged to a civilization that made a name for itself against heaven. The great city gleamed with palaces and reliefs of conquest, and thought itself eternal.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the sovereignty of God over the rise and fall of nations. He raised Assyria as the rod of His anger to chasten faithless Israel, and when its pride was full He shattered it, so that Calah and Nineveh became mounds in the wilderness. Every empire that trusts its own might and forgets the LORD is grass that withers. The city of the mighty hunter is dust; the word of God stands for ever.

Usage

"Asshur built Calah among the first cities of his empire."

"Calah stood a great city between Nineveh and Resen."

"Calah preaches that the proudest empire is grass before the LORD."
